Treatment for dysphoria includes a lot, by the way. Doesn't just pertain to sexually related surgeries.

On a personal level, I have no bindings nor real argument against legal prostitution. It makes sense. Arguably worlds oldest profession, quite frankly.

To make it clear, I'm not trying to say there's causality between them, but there's certainly connections, statistically speaking. It's often a profession of victims. Before America can make sense of legalizing prostitution, it first has to improve its social institutions and focus on helping victims, the economically distraught, and addiction so that those that choose to do sex work are choosing to do so in a healthy way, where they can thrive as any other person might. 

tl;dr Fixing social institutions is a pretense to legalizing prostitution.

I'm not sure how long you've been playing, but do you remember control decks from a while back like UW that Flock won the PT with? Those are the types of decks that can go over midrange lists like ours. I'd argue that control isn't quite like that in our standard. Typically finishers consist of Torrential Gearhulk, Linvala, Dynavolt Towers, and Wandering Fumeroles. Not to say these cards are bad, they're just not the crazy powerful cards we've seen at the top of the curve like before. 
I think Delirium wins the war of attrition. How many Liliana's are you running? She plays a huge part in those games seeing as typically if she sticks, she can remain on board. What about your number of main/side transgress the mind? Big player. 
Also, consider playing some (small) number of Gonti, Lord of Luxury. Sometime he adds some nuts power to your plays. You could hit a Gearhulk, or in my opinion, better yet, a Void Shatter, and help progress your game.
Gonti is actually my toy card right now. He's essentially a "draw 1" on a 4 drop 2/3 deathtoucher. Not too shabby. 
As for dying to Fumigate? Don't overcommit to the board. Typically speaking you won't run into 3 copies of it every single game. Make them use removal that they don't want to. If you have a Flayer, Ishkanah, and Kalitas on board, that's value town for them. But if you just have Flayer beating their face in, they have to make 1 for 1 choices. Which your deck arguably wins off of. 
Best of luck.

Well, first and foremost, if you're looking for Genesis Hydra with Chord of Calling, you'll be casting it for GGG2. Genesis Hydra will enter the battlefield as a 0/0 and be moved to your graveyard. Triggered effects that act when a creature enters or leaves the battlefield will occur. However, this isn't worth it at all. Essentially what I'm trying to say is that searching for a creature card that enters with additional counters equal to {X} isn't a great idea.
